body.statement: As a direct target-compatibility corollary, on the fixed order \(\pi=(1,2,3)\), \(\operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v)\) returns \(v=B_{\pi,32}\). For the same \(P\in\mathcal P_+\), the causal effect identified in Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.5, is defined as this same structural coordinate.
body.justification: This bookkeeping corollary records target compatibility and requires no independent fourth-order root solve.
body.gap: The published fourth-order result and the cubic inverse use different information, so their common structural coordinate must be stated without treating equality of targets as a new identification theorem.
body.consumer: The compatibility remark preserves the treatment-to-outcome interpretation when the cubic chart is used in the published workflow.
body.proof_tex:
On the fixed order \(\pi=(1,2,3)\), the definition
\[
B_\pi(u,v)=u e_2e_1^{\mathsf T}+v e_3e_2^{\mathsf T}
\]
gives \((B_\pi)_{32}=v\).  The global cubic inverse theorem proves, rather than defines, the observable-to-structural equality
\[
\operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v),
\]
so its returned \((3,2)\) coordinate is \(v\).

The cited published target-coordinate record states that Theorem 3.5 of Tramontano et al. uses the structural edge coefficient \(b_{Y,T}\) from treatment \(T\) to outcome \(Y\) as its causal target.  In the fixed published mixing map, \(T\) and \(Y\) are observed nodes \(2\) and \(3\), and the coefficient on \(2\to3\) is \(\beta\).  Matching the same structural graph to \(\pi=(1,2,3)\) therefore gives
\[
b_{Y,T}=\beta=(B_\pi)_{32}=v.
\]
This establishes equality of the structural targets; it does not assert that the published fourth-order identifying procedure and the present cubic recovery functional are the same observable map.
